body_markdown:
**Coronation Street** is set to tackle an important and rarely discussed health issue as popular character Kit Green faces a devastating breast cancer diagnosis in upcoming episodes.


The ITV soap has confirmed that Kit, played by Jacob Roberts, will be at the centre of a storyline exploring male breast cancer, a condition that many people may not realise can affect men.


The storyline is expected to begin airing in September and will follow Kit as he comes to terms with the shocking news, undergoes treatment and deals with the emotional impact the diagnosis has on both his identity and his family.


According to ITV, the storyline has been developed with support from **Macmillan Cancer Support** and **Breast Cancer Now** to ensure that the subject is portrayed responsibly and accurately.


## Kit Green receives a shocking diagnosis


Kit's health scare develops alongside a wider family discovery.


After the death of his estranged Aunt Celeste, Kit's family learns that they may carry a familial BRCA gene mutation. His mother Bernie and half-sister Gemma are subsequently faced with genetic testing as the family begins to understand the potential implications of their history.


However, Kit has already been seeking medical advice because of concerns about his own health.


What follows is a devastating revelation. Kit learns that he has stage three breast cancer.


The diagnosis is particularly shocking because breast cancer is commonly associated with women, meaning many men may not immediately consider it when they notice a change in their chest.


For Kit, the news is expected to have a profound effect. The character will reportedly struggle to understand how the illness could have happened to him and what it means for his future.


Jacob Roberts, who plays Kit, has previously said that he himself was unaware that men could develop breast cancer before becoming involved with the storyline. That experience helped shape the character's reaction, with Kit also expected to be shocked by the diagnosis.


## Why the storyline matters


Male breast cancer is rare, but it is real.


ITV says that almost 500 men in the UK face the disease each year. Male breast cancer represents less than one per cent of breast cancer cases, which can contribute to a lack of awareness.


The NHS states that breast cancer can affect anyone because everyone has some breast tissue in the chest. However, the condition is much less common in men.


That rarity can make the disease particularly difficult for some men to recognise.


A man who discovers a lump or another unusual change may assume it is something harmless or unrelated to cancer. Embarrassment can also prevent some people from speaking to a doctor.


This is one of the reasons why storylines such as Kit's can have an important public awareness role.


By showing a familiar character dealing with the condition, Coronation Street can encourage viewers to think about their own health and become more comfortable discussing symptoms.


## What are the symptoms of breast cancer in men?


The NHS advises men to be aware of changes affecting their chest, breasts and nipples.


Possible symptoms can include a lump or swelling in the chest or armpit, nipple discharge, changes in the size or shape of the chest, sores or ulcers, and changes to the appearance of the nipple.


A nipple may become inverted or develop a rash.


Importantly, experiencing one of these symptoms does not automatically mean that someone has cancer. Many chest or breast changes can have other causes.


However, the NHS recommends speaking to a GP about any unusual changes.


Early medical advice can be important because, if a symptom is linked to cancer, finding the disease earlier can make it easier to treat.


The NHS also recommends becoming familiar with what is normal for your own chest. Regularly checking for changes can make it easier to notice something unusual.


## The importance of the BRCA connection


Kit's storyline also introduces the subject of inherited cancer risk.


BRCA1 and BRCA2 are genes associated with increased risks of certain cancers. A harmful inherited change in one of these genes can increase a person's lifetime risk of developing particular cancers.


The NHS notes that men with a family history of breast or ovarian cancer may be more likely to have an inherited faulty BRCA gene.


This does not mean that everyone with a family history will develop cancer. Genetic risk is only one factor, and individual circumstances can vary considerably.


However, a significant family history may lead doctors to consider genetic counselling or testing.


Coronation Street's storyline therefore has the potential to highlight another important message: family medical history can be relevant to everyone's health, not only women's health.


## Kit's journey will go beyond the diagnosis


The soap's storyline is not simply about revealing that Kit has cancer.


Viewers will reportedly see the character deal with denial, treatment and the wider emotional consequences of his diagnosis.


That could make the storyline particularly significant because cancer affects more than the person receiving the diagnosis.


Family members can experience fear, uncertainty and guilt, particularly when questions about inherited risk are involved.


Kit's story is also expected to explore his sense of identity. A cancer diagnosis can challenge the way someone sees themselves, particularly when the illness is associated in popular culture with another gender.


Producer Kate Brooks said the diagnosis will shake the foundations of Kit's life and that the show wants to encourage people to speak to their GP if they notice changes.


Breast Cancer Now has also praised the importance of raising awareness and encouraging men to check their chest regularly.


## Coronation Street continues its tradition of tackling serious subjects


The soap has a long history of incorporating serious health issues into its storylines.


Over the years, Coronation Street has explored several different forms of cancer and other major illnesses through its characters. These plots can give viewers an opportunity to learn about conditions while following the emotional experiences of characters they already know.


Kit's storyline takes that approach into an area that remains relatively unfamiliar to many people.


The fact that the character is a man is central to the story because it challenges the misconception that breast cancer is exclusively a women's disease.


For many viewers, seeing Kit react with disbelief may also feel relatable. The shock surrounding his diagnosis reflects the reality that awareness of male breast cancer remains comparatively low.


## A storyline that could encourage men to speak up


Perhaps the most important message from Kit's story is that men should not ignore changes to their bodies.


A lump, swelling, nipple discharge or another unusual change does not necessarily mean cancer. But it should not automatically be dismissed either.


Seeking medical advice can provide reassurance when a symptom is harmless and can help ensure appropriate investigations when further assessment is needed.


The NHS says that anyone with unusual changes to their chest or nipples should contact their GP.


Through Kit Green's experience, Coronation Street is bringing that message into millions of living rooms and placing male breast cancer firmly in the conversation.


The storyline may be dramatic, emotional and difficult to watch at times, but its wider impact could be significant.


By making male breast cancer part of an established soap's narrative, Coronation Street is helping challenge misconceptions and reminding viewers that cancer does not always look the way they expect.


For Kit, the diagnosis will change his life. For viewers, his story could provide a valuable reminder to pay attention to their health and seek help when something does not feel right.

### Disclaimer


This article is intended for general information and entertainment purposes only. It is not medical advice and should not be used to diagnose or treat any health condition. Anyone concerned about a lump, swelling, nipple discharge or another unusual change should speak to a qualified healthcare professional. Medical information can change, so readers should consult official NHS guidance or their healthcare provider for current advice.
